Art. 40 gives anyone who suffers damage from any PDPL violation a right to compensation before the competent court. That is a general damages right, which GBRIEF defines as 'yes' (Kenya's s.65 is rated 'yes' on the same basis); lack of case law does not make it narrow.

checked.claim: limited: Art. 40 ... depends on proving damage
checked.replacement: yes: Art. 40 lets anyone who suffers damage from a PDPL violation claim compensation before the competent court. Damage must be proved and there is no published case law.

notes: No factual errors found, but every check rests on secondary sources (Profectus, Securiti); the PDPL text and Implementing Regulations were not retrieved, so Art. 38 confiscation, the 5-day response window and the appeal route and 60-day deadline remain unconfirmed. Securiti says the 48 decisions were issued 'in 2025', consistent with a January 2026 announcement. Main change: map.private_action should be 'yes' under the GBRIEF definition for consistency with Kenya.
